source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 31ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο πρίγκιπας»

attestations.note: The page gives him a full political life: son of St Daniel, prince of Moscow, whose day it puts at 4 March; first named in the liturgical Menaia of Novgorod between 1296 and 1297; back in Moscow probably by 1299; after his father's death in 1303 obliged to support his brother George, whom he later succeeded; retook Pereyaslavl in 1304 or 1305; allied with the princes of Rostov, Belozersk and Yaroslavl between 1320 and 1326; sent his army against Pskov in 1329; received the title of grand prince from the khan in 1331; accused Alexander of Tver before the Golden Horde in 1339 and carried the bells of the cathedral of the Saviour from Tver to Moscow; began the cathedral of the Dormition on 4 August 1326 on the advice of the aged Metropolitan Peter, and after Peter's death moved his canonisation by sending the Synod of Vladimir a letter of the wonders at his tomb in 1327. It gives the repose as «στις 31 Μαρτίου 1340 ή 1341 μ.Χ.», after he had already become a monk with the name Ananias, and the burial in the cathedral of the Archangel in the Kremlin. It prints no hymn. The corpus keeps two folders named for a Peter of Moscow and it is not certain from this page which is the metropolitan of the story, so he is named in the life without a link.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding menologion day (30 September 2026).

birth.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε περί το έτος 1290 μ.Χ.» The page's «περί», about, is why the display says about 1290.

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Ιωάννης κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη στις 31 Μαρτίου 1340 ή 1341 μ.Χ., αφού ήδη είχε γίνει μοναχός παίρνοντας το όνομα Ανανίας.» The page offers the two years and chooses neither, so the interval keeps both.
